items.title: The quadratic exponential moment of a standard Gaussian

source.anchor: Appendix C.2 A3.SS2.p1; A3.SS2.p10.m1 and p10.m3; A3.Ex104.m1; A3.SS2.p10.3
source.attribution: On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling, arXiv:2610.20492v1.
source.scope: Exact radial moment and the single-row truncation bound.

items.statement: The quadratic exponential at coefficient one third is integrable under the standard Gaussian and has the exact moment below. This moment gives the single-row tail bound at the paper’s truncation threshold.
assumptions: The producer uses the canonical standard Gaussian on a finite-dimensional real inner product space \(E\) with its Borel measurable structure. Write \(m=\dim_{\mathbb R}E\).
The exponent \(m/2\) is real. The generic result covers dimension zero, in which the law is concentrated at the origin and the moment is one.
For the source application, \(d,q\in\mathbb N\) and \(2q+1<d\). The row has \(r=q+1\) standard coordinates and uses its unscaled Euclidean norm. At \(q=0\) the moment is \(\sqrt 3\).

The row tail is the mass of the strict event \(L<\|Z\|^2\) at the literal threshold \(L=2r+3\log(1000d)\). Integrability and all positivity conditions are proved inside the corresponding Lean statements.

obligations.label: Actual finite Gaussian moment used by the private one-row tail proof.

bindings.boundary: The source obligation is the radial moment in Appendix C.2 and its single-row consequence at the displayed threshold. The source works in positive row dimension. The producer also covers arbitrary finite real inner product spaces and dimension zero. The row-family law transfer, simultaneous event, shifted tail, bias, concentration, complete Fact C.6, Lemma 4.4, and both lower bounds have separate obligations. Public integration, desktop and mobile acceptance, and postmerge purification remain pending.

assumption_deltas.reason: Orthonormal coordinates preserve the norm and law. The density calculation holds in dimension zero.

assumption_deltas.reason: A finite expectation of this nonnegative observable entails integrability.
